nodes.title: Cloudflare Pingora
nodes.summary: Rust async proxy framework, Apache-2.0; framework not a server (you write the binary). Fails slot: no per-request isolation, no capability authz, no agent protocol, no formal claims; h2 defaults weak; HTTP/3 still unmerged.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Cloudflare production scale does not transfer to the OSS crate; CVEs say Cloudflare CDN unaffected only because ingress normalizes.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Active, 119 contributors, fast fixes; best-in-class Rust L7 base.
nodes.specifics: v0.9.0 2026-09-09; ~27.7k stars; 119 contributors; 8 published GHSA: CVE-2025-4366, CVE-2025-8671 (MadeYouReset), CVE-2026-2833 and CVE-2026-2835 (critical smuggling, fixed 0.8.0, 2026-03-05), CVE-2026-2836 (insecure-default cache key), plus 3 on 2026-10-20 (Connection-header ACL bypass, h2 :authority/Host mismatch cache poisoning, h2 unbounded default header-list memory exhaustion). Issue #95 HTTP/3 open since 2024-03-02, 107 reactions. Kani/proptest/libfuzzer greps in repo: 0 hits (GitHub code search 2026-10-24).

nodes.title: River (ISRG Prossimo)
nodes.summary: Pingora-based Rust reverse proxy; effectively dormant: last commit 2024-09-06, v0.5.0 2024-08-30, README 'no expectation of stability'. Fails: dormant, no isolation/authz.
nodes.specifics: Apache-2.0, ~2.35k stars, 3 contributors (API), 0 GHSA. Dormant ~25 months at 2026-10-24.

nodes.title: Envoy
nodes.summary: C++ L7 proxy, Apache-2.0, very heavy ops (xDS). Fails: C++ memory-unsafe, large CVE stream, heavy ops, no per-request isolation; but has in-tree MCP filters (mcp, mcp_router, mcp_json_rest_bridge).
nodes.specifics: v1.40.1 2026-10-23; ~29.1k stars; 1776 contributors; >=100 published GHSA (API cap; 43 since 2025-10). Issue #39174 'Envoy Support for MCP' open, 42 reactions. No formal/DST claims found.

nodes.title: NGINX (F5)
nodes.summary: C, BSD-2; the incumbent. Fails: C memory-unsafe, CVE stream continues incl. HTTP/3 and TLS ticket bugs, no isolation, no agent protocol; MCP only via njs + community issue.
nodes.specifics: 1.31.8 2026-10-21; ~32k stars; nginx.org page lists ~26 advisories with 2026 IDs (e.g. CVE-2026-95101 HTTP/3 request body injection, CVE-2026-97629 TLS session-ticket forgery, CVE-2026-97205 AIO UAF, CVE-2026-42530 HTTP/3 UAF) vs 2 with 2025 IDs. IDs are as listed by nginx.org; year counts derived from ID prefix, not publish date. OpenSSL 3.5 builds negotiate X25519MLKEM768 (Ubuntu 25.10 test, secondary).

nodes.title: NGINX Unit (archived) and FreeUnit
nodes.summary: Polyglot app server (closest historical analogue to the slot: app runtime + proxy, JSON-API config). Archived 2025-10-08; last release 1.35.0 2025-09-11. Community fork FreeUnit (v1.37.0 2026-10-04, 70 stars, 75 contributors, Apache-2.0) adds OTel, Wasm component (WASI 0.2). Fails: C, no isolation, abandoned by vendor.
nodes.specifics: README: 'Unsupported... security vulnerabilities may be unaddressed'. FreeBSD port expiry 2025-12-31 (search result, secondary).

nodes.title: Caddy
nodes.summary: Go, Apache-2.0, auto-HTTPS single binary; strongest household ergonomics. Fails: Go GC runtime, no per-request isolation, plugin supply chain, no capability authz, no agent protocol.
nodes.specifics: v2.11.7 2026-10-03; ~78.4k stars; 465 contributors; 18 GHSA. Go 1.24 crypto/tls enables X25519MLKEM768 by default (kubernetes.dev PQC blog); a Caddy community thread reports a reverse-proxy transport still negotiating X25519 (unresolved), so Caddy PQ default per-path is B.

nodes.title: Traefik
nodes.summary: Go, MIT; cloud-native router. Fails: Go, >=89 GHSA (API cap 100), label/Docker coupling, no isolation. Gains share from ingress-nginx retirement.

nodes.title: HAProxy
nodes.summary: C, GPL/LGPL mix (GitHub: NOASSERTION); highest-performance L4/L7 LB. Fails: C, no app tier, no isolation; QUIC parse CVEs 2026-02.
nodes.specifics: 3.4.7 LTS (support to 2031-Q2); CVE-2026-26080/26081 QUIC crash fixed 2026-02-12 (3.0.12/3.1.14/3.2.12/3.3.3); issue #3515 jwt_verify accepted alg=none (closed 2026-09-29). 0 published GHSA on GitHub.

nodes.title: Ferron
nodes.summary: Rust MIT web server (2.2k stars, 23 contributors); closest 'Rust nginx replacement'. Seven high/critical advisories on one day 2026-09-25 (h2 Rapid Reset bypass, h3 SETTINGS O(n^2), auth_to fail-open critical, forward-proxy ACL fail-open) show immaturity; v3.0 still rc (3.0.0-rc.10).
nodes.underclaim_risk: Fast response; reported via coordinated batch.
nodes.specifics: stable 2.8.1 2026-06-17; 7 GHSA. cargo-fuzz in tree (4 hits). Evidence that a young Rust server re-learns classic bugs (fail-open authz, Rapid Reset).

nodes.title: Sozu
nodes.summary: Rust hot-reconfigurable proxy, AGPL-3.0 (licence blocks many enterprises), 3.7k stars, 64 contributors, 2.3.3 2026-10-19, 0 GHSA. Fails: AGPL, no isolation/authz/agent protocol.

nodes.title: 2025-26 Rust proxy entrants: Pingoo, Aralez, pingora-proxy-manager
nodes.summary: Pingoo (MIT, 1.0k stars, built-in WAF/bot/PQ-TLS, no release tag, 0 GHSA, README markets against 'Enterprise Edition' paywalls); Aralez (Pingora-based, Apache-2.0, 804 stars, v0.95.2 2026-10-21, 7 contributors). No Zig server >300 stars found (GitHub search). All single-maintainer-scale; none claim isolation or verification.

nodes.title: Spin / SpinKube (Fermyon -> Akamai)
nodes.summary: Wasmtime-based per-request component host; Apache-2.0, CNCF (SpinKube); Akamai acquired Fermyon 2025-12-01. Fails: it is a FaaS framework, not a front server; needs separate ingress; no capability authz beyond WASI allow-lists; vendor now an edge CDN.
nodes.specifics: v4.2.5 2026-10-23; 6.55k stars; 100 contributors; 2 GHSA (CVE-2024-32980 critical network sandbox escape; CVE-2026-27887 memory leaks). Instantiation latency claims are vendor-only ('under a millisecond', 2022).

nodes.title: wasmCloud, WasmEdge, Wasmer, workerd, Fastly Viceroy
nodes.summary: wasmCloud v2.11.0 (2.46k stars, 0 GHSA); WasmEdge 0.18.1 (10.8k, 1 GHSA); Wasmer 7.5.0 (21k, MIT, 9 GHSA); workerd v1.20261025.1 (9k, C++/V8, 2 old GHSA) whose README states it is NOT a hardened sandbox and must run inside a VM; Viceroy 0.21.1 is a local Fastly Compute simulator. Fastly datasheet claims per-request isolation with few-microsecond instantiation (vendor claim).
nodes.specifics: Wasmer Edge status could not be established (wasmer.io blog 404; no news found) -> E for its commercial status.

nodes.title: Wasmtime advisory stream and LLM-found bugs
nodes.summary: Wasmtime v50.0.0 (2026-10-20): 81 published GHSA (7 critical, 6 high, 45 medium, 23 low; 60 published since 2025-10). On 2026-04-09 the project shipped 12 advisories at once (2 critical sandbox escapes CVE-2026-34987 Winch and CVE-2026-34971 Cranelift aarch64); 11/12 found by the team's LLM multi-agent harness; continuous fuzzing does not cover aarch64 for Cranelift/Winch. Implies: Wasm is a strong but not absolute boundary, and AI-driven bug discovery is already shifting advisory rates.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Counting advisories penalizes the project that finds its own bugs.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Critical sandbox escapes exist in shipped Tier-1 compilers; 'absolute isolation' framing is wrong.
nodes.specifics: Counts from GitHub security-advisories API 2026-10-24 (published only).

nodes.title: Hyperlight (hyperlight-dev, CNCF Sandbox)
nodes.summary: Rust hypervisor-backed function sandbox (Apache-2.0, 4.76k stars, v0.18.0 2026-10-14, 34 contributors, 1 GHSA low). Microsoft claims ~0.9 ms per call (KubeCon demo, Rust guest) and 1-2 ms for Hyperlight Wasm (experimental). Fails: library not server; no network stack/ingress; vendor numbers only. Repo has cargo-fuzz/libfuzzer targets; no Kani/Verus hits.

nodes.title: Firecracker
nodes.summary: Rust microVM monitor, Apache-2.0, v1.17.0 2026-09-10, 37.6k stars, 304 contributors, 2 GHSA (CVE-2026-5747 virtio-pci OOB write high; CVE-2026-1386 jailer symlink). Has Kani proofs in tree (17 code-search hits). Fails: ~125ms-class VM boot, needs KVM (not on $5 VPS without nested virt), not a server.
nodes.specifics: Boot-time figures not re-measured here (E for numbers).

nodes.title: Unikraft / Unikraft Cloud
nodes.summary: Unikraft OSS RELEASE-0.21.0 2026-05-20 (3.9k stars, licence NOASSERTION/BSD mix), 0 GHSA. Unikraft Cloud: $6M seed 2025-10-09; vendor claims <10 ms cold start, 100K+ density. Fails: POSIX-app compat, hosted dependency, vendor-only numbers; independent 2026 adoption evidence not found.

nodes.title: Lunatic
nodes.summary: Erlang-style Wasm actor runtime; dormant: last release v0.13.2 2023-05-03, last commit 2025-03-29, 4.9k stars, 0 GHSA. Fails: abandoned.

nodes.title: Deno and Bun
nodes.summary: Deno v2.9.8 (MIT, 108.8k stars, 40 GHSA, permission flags are the closest mainstream capability model but process-wide). Bun v1.4.4 (96k stars, 3 GHSA, licence NOASSERTION): Rust rewrite merged 2026-05-14 per bun.com; Anthropic acquired Bun Dec 2025 (bun.com, secondary elsewhere); Zig author published critique. Fail: JS runtimes, no per-request isolation, GC.
nodes.specifics: Bun Rust claims (99.8% tests) from secondary source only.

nodes.title: Encore, Convex, PostgREST/Supabase, Hasura
nodes.summary: Encore v1.58.8 (Go, MPL-2.0, 6 GHSA); convex-backend (FSL-Apache, source-available, SQLite/Postgres, 1 GHSA; self-host lacks SSO/RBAC/audit per third-party claims, unverified); PostgREST v16.5 (Haskell, MIT, 0 GHSA, DB-as-API with RLS); Supabase (113.9k stars, Apache-2.0); Hasura v2.51.2 (v2 LTS to 2027-01-01 EOL for 2.45, DDN v3 CLI/console proprietary per third party). Fail: each binds to one DB or one app model; none is a general middle tier with isolation.

nodes.title: Docker MCP Gateway
nodes.summary: Go, MIT, container-per-server isolation. v0.44.2, 1.6k stars, 39 contributors, 10 GHSA incl. 2 critical on 2026-07-09 (unauthenticated access to proxied tools in container mode CVE-2026-76092; config-driven bind mount CVE-2026-76099), image signature verification off by default (CVE-2026-76094), tool-name shadowing (CVE-2026-76097), DNS rebinding CVE-2025-64443, case-variant reserved-name bypass 2026-10-13. Shows gateways ship insecure defaults and re-learn confused-deputy bugs.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Advisories mean transparency not worse security.
nodes.underclaim_risk: A flagship security gateway shipped with unauthenticated tool access in a supported mode.

nodes.title: agentgateway (Linux Foundation, Solo.io)
nodes.summary: Rust data plane for MCP/A2A/LLM, Apache-2.0, v1.6.0 2026-10-02, 5.5k stars, 280 contributors, 5 GHSA incl. high 'stateful MCP sessions can cross routes and overwrite the authorization policy' (2026-07-27) and MCP-to-OpenAPI parameter sanitization (CVE-2026-29791). The strongest OSS candidate in the agent-protocol column; fails: no formal claims, no isolation of tool handlers (it proxies), policy is CEL-like config not proof-backed.
nodes.specifics: cargo-fuzz in tree (2 hits); madsim 0 hits.

nodes.title: Envoy AI Gateway, renamed Agent Router
nodes.summary: envoyproxy/ai-gateway now redirects to theagentrouter/agent-router ('Formerly Envoy AI Gateway', Agentic AI Foundation project), Go, Apache-2.0, v1.2.0 2026-10-07, 2.3k stars, 165 contributors. Envoy core also has in-tree mcp, mcp_router, mcp_json_rest_bridge filters. Fails: Envoy ops weight, C++ data plane.

nodes.title: Cloudflare MCP Server Portals
nodes.summary: Hosted Zero Trust MCP aggregator (launched Aug 2025, beta, requires Cloudflare Access and AI Controls); not self-hostable, so fails sovereignty/household/gov on-prem.

nodes.title: Other MCP/AI gateways: Kong, Tyk, IBM ContextForge, Bifrost, ToolHive, Pomerium, Lasso, Microsoft mcp-gateway, Invariant/Snyk
nodes.summary: Kong (Lua, Apache-2.0, 44k stars; MCP proxy plugin since 3.12 Oct 2025; third parties say governance is enterprise-tier, unverified); Tyk (licence NOASSERTION); IBM mcp-context-forge (Python, v1.1.0, 19 GHSA); Bifrost (Go, 9k stars, enterprise build); ToolHive (Go, v0.56.0, 43 GHSA); Pomerium (Go, v0.33.4, 13 GHSA); Lasso mcp-gateway (Python, last release 2026-01-21, 5 contributors); microsoft/mcp-gateway (C#, no release); Invariant acquired by Snyk 2025-06 (scanner now Snyk Agent Scan). Pattern: many are Python/Go/TS, container-per-server, with large advisory counts.

nodes.title: Agent firewalls and sandboxes: pipelock, nono, mcpdef, ThinkWatch
nodes.summary: pipelock (Go, Apache-2.0, 959 stars, v3.7.1, signed hash-chained action receipts, 5 GHSA); nono (Rust, Apache-2.0, 4.7k stars, v0.80.0, process sandbox for agents, 12 GHSA); ThinkWatch (Rust, 819 stars, licence NOASSERTION, 3 contributors); mcpdef (Rust Wasm sandbox, appears only on Docker Hub, unverified E). Most are client-side or egress-side; none is a server tier that also hosts handlers.

nodes.title: Unserved: one memory-safe binary combining front proxy, per-request isolated handlers, capability authz and agent protocols
nodes.summary: No surveyed project combines (a) memory-safe single binary, (b) per-request hardware/Wasm isolation, (c) capability-style authorization checked at the boundary, (d) native MCP/A2A/agent-identity handling, (e) PQ-TLS by default, (f) any machine-checked claim. Proxies lack b,c; Wasm hosts lack front-proxy and c; MCP gateways lack b and f. Absence claim: based on this survey only (grade C).
nodes.overclaim_risk: Absence of evidence in a ~45-repo survey is not proof no private/closed product exists.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Pieces exist in production (Spin per-request isolation, agentgateway MCP, Pingora/rustls PQ); the gap is integration and assurance.

nodes.title: Unserved: no surveyed server makes machine-checked or DST claims
nodes.summary: In-tree grep (GitHub code search 2026-10-24): Kani present only in Firecracker (17 hits); no Verus hits in hyperlight/wasmtime/others; no turmoil/madsim in the proxies checked (agentgateway madsim 0); fuzzing exists in hyperlight, ferron, sozu, agentgateway (cargo-fuzz/libfuzzer). Web search found no 2025-26 verified HTTP server/proxy; Cedar (Dafny) is authz only. Search tool limits make this C.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Code search is keyword-only and rate-limited; some claims may live in docs/CI not matched.

nodes.title: Pattern: gateways and young servers fail open and ship insecure defaults
nodes.summary: Evidence: Docker MCP Gateway (unauth proxied tools; sig verification off by default), Ferron auth_to fail-open critical, forward-proxy DNS/ACL fail-open, Pingora insecure-by-default cache key and unbounded h2 header-list default, agentgateway session policy overwrite. Implies a fail-closed-by-construction requirement and a default-config gate in CI.

nodes.title: Pattern: maintenance churn and acquisitions in this tier
nodes.summary: NGINX Unit archived 2025-10-08; River dormant since 2024-09; Lunatic dormant; ingress-nginx retired 2026-03 with InGate dropped; Fermyon->Akamai 2025-12; Invariant->Snyk 2025-06; Bun->Anthropic 2025-12; Envoy AI Gateway renamed. Users bear migration risk, so governance (foundation home, multiple maintainers) is a selection criterion.

nodes.title: Demand signals: what people say they would switch for
nodes.summary: (1) ingress-nginx retired, official statement says no drop-in replacement (kubernetes.io 2026-01-29). (2) Pingora HTTP/3 request, 107 reactions, open 2.6 years. (3) Envoy MCP proposal 42 reactions. (4) Stacklok survey Jul 2026 (n=100 enterprise engineers): 41% some production MCP, only 5% governed enterprise-wide; WorkOS: 18% implement tool scoping (secondary); Adversa scan 38% of 500 servers no auth on critical endpoints (secondary, via blog). (5) Self-hosters pick Caddy for simple config/auto-HTTPS, Traefik for Docker labels (forum threads). (6) Pingoo README complains of paywalled Enterprise features. Most evidence is thin: forum threads, vendor blogs, one n=100 survey (grade C).
nodes.overclaim_risk: Vendor/blog sourced stats; reactions are not purchases.
nodes.underclaim_risk: No instrument measures willingness-to-switch at household scale.

nodes.title: PQ-TLS posture of incumbents
nodes.summary: Hybrid X25519MLKEM768 reachable by default via Go 1.24 (Caddy/Traefik builds), OpenSSL 3.5 (nginx builds on Ubuntu 25.10/26.04 per Canonical discourse), Pingoo advertises PQ-TLS; Envoy status not established; PQ authentication (ML-DSA certs) not a differentiator yet. So 'PQ key exchange' alone does not fill the slot.

edges.note: Rust MCP data plane vs Envoy filters

seeds.question: Do rustls/aws-lc-rs-based proxies (Pingora rustls feature, agentgateway) negotiate X25519MLKEM768 by default and what is the measured handshake cost on a 1-vCPU VPS?
Measure Wasmtime pooling-allocator per-request instantiate latency and RSS vs Hyperlight vs process fork+seccomp on same hardware (independent of vendor numbers).
seeds.reason: all isolation latency figures are vendor claims

seeds.question: Read the 2026-07-27 agentgateway GHSA (session overwrite authz) and docker/mcp-gateway CVE-2026-76092 diffs: derive the invariant each violated and whether a type/capability boundary would have prevented it.
Does any server or gateway ship Cedar/OPA/CEL policy with SMT-checked analysis in the request path (agentgateway CEL, Envoy, Pomerium)?
Primary-source check of Pingora HTTP/3 timeline, rustls-vs-OpenSSL backends, and FIPS status; same for River succession.
seeds.reason: Pingora is likely base candidate; open h3 gap

seeds.question: Quantify willingness-to-switch: mine Reddit/HN/lobste.rs threads (not mirrors) on ingress-nginx replacement and MCP gateway selection; classify stated criteria.
Verify Wasmer Edge, Unikraft Cloud and Hyperlight Wasm production status and independent benchmarks.
Compare LLM-found vs human-found advisory rates across Wasmtime/Pingora/Envoy 2025-26 to estimate time-to-exploit shift.

protocol_implications: Selection criteria from gap data: foundation-hosted or multi-maintainer base, fail-closed defaults gate, secure-by-default config tested in CI (insecure-defaults pattern).
Wasm is a strong but breakable boundary (Wasmtime 2 critical escapes 2026-04, 81 advisories): design needs defense in depth (OS sandbox) and rapid patch pipeline; do not claim absolute isolation.

MCP gateway reference tests: session-cross-route policy overwrite (agentgateway), tool-name shadowing/case variants, unauthenticated proxied tools, DNS rebinding (docker/mcp-gateway) become regression fixtures.
HTTP conformance corpus must include Pingora/nginx 2026 smuggling and h2/h3 DoS cases (CVE-2026-2833/2835, MadeYouReset, Rapid Reset bypass, h3 SETTINGS O(n^2)).
Positioning: gap is integration plus assurance, not any single feature; every competitor lacks machine-checked claims, so claims must be scoped to proved components only.
self_improvement: GitHub API (gh api repos/*, security-advisories, search/code) gives A-grade metadata cheaply; add a reusable script to tools/ for repo metadata+GHSA counts; code search is rate-limited to ~10/min and returns errors that look like '{'.
WebSearch snippets are lossy; always follow with primary fetch for versions/CVEs. Search tool ignores quoted operators; mirror sites (reddit.sentinel-team) pollute results.
GHSA 'published' count undercounts project CVEs (nginx publishes none on GitHub); require per-project advisory source in schema.
